nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox testing costs
Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (compute, storage) - monthly estimate x project duration
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licensing (if needed)
Contingency buffer for unforeseen integration issues (10% of labour)

assumptions: Rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: all 24 backlog items are costed against a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE available. This is indicative only and MUST be revisited once real team roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, DevOps, PM) and their individual rates are assigned.

With only 1 FTE available, the team can deliver roughly 2,080 productive hours/year (minus ~15% for meetings/overhead ≈ 1,750-1,800 usable hours/year). The estimated 2,867 hours implies this backlog cannot be completed by a single FTE within one year; it would take approximately 1.6-1.7 years of solo effort, or the client should add headcount/roles once the rate card is finalized.

Story points were converted to engineering hours using a rough heuristic of 1 point ≈ 11-12 hours (covering design, build, test, review, deployment), consistent with typical small-to-mid complexity full-stack web tasks; actual conversion will vary once true team composition and velocity data exist.

No historical actuals (real spend or velocity data) exist for this project yet, so all effort figures are estimates based on task descriptions and industry-typical complexity for similar SaaS/customer-portal features, not on empirical throughput.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as high-risk/high-effort due to volume (400k customers, 2M invoice lines) and potential schema mismatches; extra buffer time is embedded in its hour allocation.

Payment integration (PW-7) and RBAC (PW-4) are assumed to require additional security/compliance diligence beyond raw feature-build time, reflected in higher per-point hour multipliers for those items.
CI/staging setup (PW-1) is treated as a prerequisite and front-loaded in the schedule, though costed as normal effort.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for infrastructure, tooling and audits; no vendor quotes have been obtained.
Priority breakdown costs are calculated by summing the labour cost proportionally allocated to tasks in each priority bucket, based on points-weighted hour estimates.

A single-FTE staffing model as given is almost certainly insufficient for a project of this scope (24 tasks, 178 story points); this estimate assumes the client will scale the team once real rate-card roles are defined, and the given total should be read as 'cost per unit of effort' rather than a deliverable timeline for 1 person.
input.reasoning: "Total backlog is 178 story points across 24 tasks. Using an approximate 11-12 hours-per-point heuristic (adjusted upward for high-risk/compliance items like payments, RBAC, and data migration, and downward for simpler UI/config tasks), total effort was estimated at ~2,867 hours. This was costed against the only available rate-card role, 'Team member' at $75/hour flat, yielding a most-likely total of ~$215,000 in labour. A 10th/90th percentile spread of roughly -20%/+28% was applied to reflect the substantial estimation uncertainty inherent in point-based sizing without historical velocity data, and the added risk from complex items (payment integration, legacy migration, multi-currency, RBAC). Non-labour costs were added as conservative placeholders for infrastructure, tooling, and audits, plus a 10% labour contingency buffer given the lack of actuals. Priority breakdown apportions labour cost by summing estimated hours for tasks in each priority tier (Urgent: PW-3, PW-7; High: PW-1, PW-4, PW-5, PW-8, PW-9, PW-17; Medium: PW-2, PW-6, PW-10 through PW-16 excl. PW-17, PW-20, PW-21, PW-22; Low: PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24), multiplied by the $75/hr rate."

reductions.description: Descope Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase; these total 39 points (~22% of backlog).
reductions.effect: Removes ~390 hours of labour from initial delivery; can be revisited as a phase 2 backlog once core portal is live.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) to single-currency (USD) launch, deferring EUR/PLN support until post-launch demand is confirmed.
reductions.effect: Cuts estimated 156 hours of FX-rate integration, settlement logic and multi-currency QA from the initial release.

reductions.description: Simplify Legacy data migration (PW-8) scope to a phased/incremental migration (e.g. migrate active accounts first, archive rest) rather than a full big-bang migration of all 400k records and 2M invoice lines up front.
reductions.effect: Reduces initial migration engineering and validation effort by roughly 30%, deferring bulk historical data migration to a later maintenance window.

reductions.description: Defer Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA (PW-15) and Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) until after initial launch, doing only minimal baseline compliance/logging at launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~160 hours of polish/instrumentation work from the critical path; both are important but not launch-blocking if a fast-follow release is planned within weeks.

reductions.description: Delay third-party accessibility audit and reduce staging/CI infra spend by using a smaller single-environment setup initially instead of full staging parity.
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour spend; full audit and infra scale-up can happen once user traffic materializes.
